To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Society of Abatominal Radiology Disease-Focused Panel on RCC has been functional for over 4 years and has made substantial progress in improving patient care, education and research in this disease.

the DFP program has been a successful vehicle for multi-institutional research in RCC and has created new knowledge that has been disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and presentations at SAR and other national and international meetings.
the DFP on RCC has been active in clinical, research, educational, and advocacy activities to optimize the care, diagnosis, and management of patients with known and suspected RCC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel biomarkers that will improve patient care, education and research in the field of RCC.
improving the care of patients through a better understanding of their disease and the application of that understanding to improve the care of patients.
the identification, characterization, and treatment of renal cell carcinoma (kidney cancer).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SAR DFP program is working to improve the care of patients by improving the understanding and treatment of RCC.
the RCC DFP has been successful in achieving its mission and has the potential to expand its mission to other aspects of renal cancer in the future.
the RCC DFP has been a success, but that it will need to evolve to meet the needs of the changing landscape of RCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DFP on RCC has been active in many projects and has been successful in creating a forum to improve patient care and research.
the DFP is a successful mechanism for improving patient care, education and research in a particular disease or a particular aspects of a disease.
the RCC DFP has been successful in creating a multi-institutional collaborative effort that has resulted in several clinical, research, educational, and advocacy projects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
collaboration between radiologists, oncologists, pathologists, urologists, and basic science researchers is critical for the advancement of patient care and scientific knowledge in this disease.
multi-disciplinary and multi-institutional collaboration has been a key to our success.
the DFP model is a useful tool for the SAR and its members.
